label: Self-hosted incident management
headline: Bring incident operations onto your infrastructure.
description: Keep operational data and deployment decisions under your control. Connect alerts to on-call, response, customer updates and postmortems.
problem: You need a complete response workflow and the ability to decide where the system runs.
workflow: Deploy an integrated runtime, connect an inbound provider, configure schedules and routing, then validate one synthetic incident end to end.

label: SRE teams
headline: Close the loop on reliability.
description: Connect the alert to the response, the response to the review, and the review to owned follow-up work.
problem: A restored service is only part of the job. Response evidence and learning need to survive the incident.
workflow: Track incident ownership and SLA outcomes, review MTTA and MTTR, and create a postmortem with action items assigned to owners.

label: Platform engineering
headline: Build a shared response foundation.
description: Give service teams a common incident workflow while keeping deployment, identity and operational health in view.
problem: Different teams own different services, but the incident platform still needs coherent access and operational control.
workflow: Organize teams and services, connect OIDC and SCIM, and use worker health and delivery evidence to operate the platform.

label: Regulated environments
headline: Keep control and evidence together.
description: Run the data plane yourself. Apply identity and authorization controls and review operational evidence in your own environment.
problem: Your response tooling must fit your data handling, access and retention requirements.
workflow: Plan the deployment, configure scoped roles and identity, review audit events, and use privacy and evidence workflows for your own controls.

label: On-call operations
headline: Make responsibility explicit.
description: Build schedules, apply overrides and route escalation to the responder responsible for the service.
problem: Coverage and handoffs are hard to reason about during a page.
workflow: Create rotations, validate current coverage, configure escalation targets and confirm delivery outcomes on a test incident.

label: DevOps teams
headline: Connect your monitoring to the response.
description: Bring signals from your existing tools into a shared incident lifecycle.
problem: Alerts arrive from several tools, while ownership and communication happen elsewhere.
workflow: Connect providers, map services and escalation policies, coordinate in ChatOps and publish scoped customer updates.
